title: What is Developmental Language Disorder (DLD)?
summary: An introduction to DLD, how it affects communication, and strengths-first approaches.

blocks.text: Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) is a common condition that affects how individuals learn and use language. People with DLD may have difficulty understanding what others say or expressing their own thoughts and ideas.
DLD is not caused by hearing loss, autism, intellectual disability, or lack of exposure to language.

Children and adults with DLD have many strengths, including creativity, problem-solving abilities, and strong visual skills. Recognizing and building upon these strengths is essential for support and confidence.
LinguaCare supports language development. It does not diagnose. Talk to a speech-language professional for formal assessment.
